title: OXO Good Grips 11-Pound Stainless Steel Food Scale with Pull-Out Display
description:
About this item
Stainless steel is smudge and fingerprint-resistant
Zero function for taring the scale before weighing additional ingredients
Digital screen with large, easy-to-read numbers
Removable platform for convenient cleaning
Pull-Out display prevents shadowing from large plates or bowls
Unit conversion button to measure in ounces, pounds, gram or kilogram
› See more product details
reviews_5s:
Love how easy this is to use. Mostly all stainless steel exterior so wipes clean easily. Display and controls pull out from the weighing platform for larger bowls. Easy to zero or tare, and easy to switch from English to Metric measurements. It is better to weigh flour than to scoop-measure it.
I'm also trying to sell some household items and knick-knacks, this makes it easy to weigh those packages to correctly charge shipping.After reading many Reddit reviews in addition to these reviews, I can definitely say they are true. This scale is awesome. As a bodybuilder and licensed nutritional coach, my scale is my #1 tool, and having had an Escali for the past 4 years, I feel like this was a real upgrade. I had the Escali because the accuracy and response time was known to be top notch, but this beats or at worst matches it, plus the size of the scale and the addition of the pullout and lighted display makes this gold. Highly recommended.Fantastic scale. Obviously the pull out display is awesome but so is the capacity of 11 lbs. Most kitchen scales are only 5. My only wish would be weighing in tenths of a gram. Otherwise, it's perfect.Oxo brand. Cant go wrong. Lightweight. Small enough to sit on counter. Color goes with kitchen appliances. Easy to functionMakes baking more fun, thx.Went by an endorsement from PBS Cooks Country on this. Made bread using the weight instead of cups measure. Easy to use and reset to 0. Goes from ounces to grams with a push button. Being able to pull out display board was convenient for oversized bowls and product. ThanksLove the scale, I use it daily, sometimes many times a day.Very nice, on time, as expected. Love the pull out digital deviceLove this scaleReally impressed with this product, 10/10 will recommend!
reviews_1s:
EDIT:
It is now February 2021 and customer service has said because I bought this product outside the US they were unable to help me in any way. They did offer to give me a discount on a more precise scale on their own website but couldn't ship it internationally to me regardless.
The customer service interaction went on so long I was eventually told I couldn't be helped just ten days after the return window for the product closed.
I have given up hope of a response from customer service which is why I am writing this review as I wanted to give them a chance to make it right. I would not recommend buying this product based on the issue I had with precision and their customer service.

I bought this product based on recommendations from chefs I admire because I wanted to take my cooking and baking more seriously. Especially when it came to small amounts of ingredients that make a big difference such as salt. When I started using it I was impressed with how quickly it turns on, and stays active but I soon realised that it is not that precise. When I tested it by weighing the same small increments repeatedly the results varied by 4g. I was dismayed because this is a pricier scale and contacted OXOs customer service to ask was this an expected margin of error or was the product I received faulty. They say on their website they will respond within 48 hours (excluding weekends to give their staff a break, an admirable approach!) but weeks later I had received no response so I emailed again. I got a response 9 days later asking for the id code of my original complaint which I provided within a day, I have heard nothing since. I have emailed their international and american customer service. My original email was on the 13th of October, my one and only follow up was on the 22nd of October. I have now contacted them 6 times either through email or their form on their website and have three separate incident numbers.With how expensive this scale is, I’m surprised that it broke so much faster than my cheaper scales. The fundamental flaw of this scale is that the battery port is very low, so even a little bit of water under your scale will damage it.

Also, every single time you turn on the scale, you have to wait 3 seconds for it to boot up. It’s owned maybe 10+ different scales in my life between kitchen scales, pocket scales, and body weight scales, and I’ve never seen a loading time on one except for this one. It is VERY annoying.The whole point of a scale is accuracy. The range on this scale is too coarse as it only shows measurements down to tenths, such as 1.2 oz. But most of my recipes ask for thirds or quarters. What if you need 1.25, 1.75, or 1.33 ounces? You have to round, throwing off the proportions. So if the recipe asks for one and a quarter ounces (1.25) you are stuck with going for 1.2 or 1.3 ounces. I guess the only work around is to use grams. I miss my old oxo scale which did show quarters and thirds. That scale was also a better size, as this scale has a small footprint.The only good thing is that it looks nice. But it doesn't work. I weigh something out and then walk away and when I've returned it's another weight. tonight I was making bread and the more flour I removed from the scale the heavier the bowl got. If you don't care about accuracy then buy this, but if you don't care about accuracy, why spend $50 on a scale?I really liked the functionality of this scale. However, it didn't even last one year. It simply failed to turn on. And yes, we changed the batteries. Honestly, my experience with just about any OXO item is similar. Bottom line: pretty to look at, functional but short lifespan. I'm done with OXO.I am very disappointed. This scale got good review, and I am wondering if I just happened to get a klunker. There was no appliance manual or booklet included in case of a troubleshooting necessity. I also didn't know whether the measurements were for fluid ounces or dry ounces. There is a pull out feature which allows the person to place a large heavy bowl on the scale (which it allowed you to zero out) in order to read the digital weight. However, the scale is inaccurate. e.g.: for 1 3/4 cups of flour, it gave me the gram weight and would give me the ounces, but still it was inaccurate. I had to re-measure with my measuring cups. I not only tried to use the weight for ounces, but I tried weighing grams. Both were inaccurate. Don't waste your money with this scale. I will be looking for a different brand.Broke in under a year. Just has “Lo” error even with batteries replaced. No damage to the scale, just not built to last. I liked the scale until now, but a year is just not a long enough lifespan.First disappointment, that I did not know until way too late to return: Does not do 10th of a gram. Ridiculous for a kitchen scale not to be accurate for baking. Next problem: It began acting weird very quickly. You put the bowl NEAR it and it changes. Literally 3 inches ABOVE it, BEFORE you even put it down on the scale, it starts reading. Like, gravity is effecting it or something. Ridiculous. OXO is overrated. Half of the things I have from them, great. The other half, not good. Sad.This scale is not accurate! I've reset the Tare on the scale to zero, measured an item then removed it, and the scale did not go back to zero. After resetting it, I let the scale sit and the measurement drifts up and down not staying steady. I also compared the weight to another scale that I know is accurate and it was off by as much as an ounce. I also noticed on the bottom of the scale it reads "Not Legal For Trade". I imagine that is an admission that the scale isn't accurate. It is a slim nice-looking scale, but unfortunately, it doesn't meet my needs. I will be looking for another one!Imagine putting a half pound object on a scale, and it still reads zero grams. Imagine it then flickering between 0 and 2 grams. You get it to work, and then the weight starts drifting by a gram every few seconds. Even if I have nothing on the scale, it might start driving positive or negative after 15 or 20 seconds.

Had an OXO food scale previously and wanted to replace it. What a mistake. Should've never got rid of my old one. This one is going back and I'm finding an entirely different manufacturer of scale to buy.
